_meta.title: SafeSiteGen machine-checkable rule pack
_meta.source: Paraphrased summaries of 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA construction standards).
_meta.disclaimer: This is an illustrative research subset for content validation, not a compliance tool. Clause text is paraphrased. Always consult the eCFR for authoritative language.

rules.topic: Fall protection: unprotected sides and edges
rules.summary: An employee on a walking or working surface with an unprotected side or edge 6 feet or more above a lower level must be protected by a guardrail system, safety net system, or personal fall arrest system.

An employee on a walking or working surface must be protected from falling through holes more than 6 feet above a lower level by personal fall arrest systems, covers, or guardrail systems erected around the hole.
The top edge height of top rails must be 42 inches plus or minus 3 inches above the walking or working level.

When a portable ladder is used to access an upper landing surface, the side rails must extend at least 3 feet above the landing, or the ladder must be secured at the top to a rigid support and a grasping device provided.
Each employee on a scaffold more than 10 feet above a lower level must be protected from falling by a guardrail system or a personal fall arrest system.

Each employee in an excavation must be protected from cave-ins by an adequate protective system, except where the excavation is made entirely in stable rock, or is less than 5 feet deep and a competent person finds no indication of a potential cave-in.
A stairway, ladder, ramp, or other safe means of egress must be located in trench excavations 4 feet or more in depth so that no more than 25 feet of lateral travel is required.

Employees must be protected from excavated material and equipment that could pose a hazard by falling or rolling into the excavation, by keeping such material at least 2 feet from the edge or by using retaining devices.

rules.topic: Cranes: power line safety, up to 350 kV
rules.summary: Before assembly or operation near a power line, the employer must either de-energise and ground the line or maintain a minimum clearance of 20 feet between the line and any part of the equipment or load, unless a smaller table-based clearance is established.

rules.topic: Cranes: keeping clear of the load
rules.summary: While the operator is not moving a suspended load, no employee may be within the fall zone except for employees engaged in hooking, unhooking, guiding the load, or performing the initial connection.

No employer may use a motor vehicle with an obstructed view to the rear unless it has a reverse signal alarm audible above the surrounding noise level, or the vehicle is backed up only when an observer signals that it is safe to do so.
Employees working in areas where there is a possible danger of head injury from impact, falling or flying objects, or electrical shock and burns must be protected by protective helmets.
All protruding reinforcing steel onto and into which employees could fall must be guarded to eliminate the hazard of impalement.
Signalling by flaggers and the use of flaggers in work zones must conform to Part VI of the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices.
